conflicts.description: carry-is-king, dollar-king, mean-reverter, perma-bear, rate-dove, rate-hawk, trend-follower expect USD higher while perma-bull expect USD lower
perma-bull, value-guy expect CAD higher while carry-is-king, dollar-king, perma-bear, rate-dove, rate-hawk, trend-follower expect CAD lower
cross-merchant, perma-bull expect NZD higher while dollar-king, perma-bear, rate-dove, trend-follower expect NZD lower

own_pitch.stance_summary: Verified: Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 16 Sep, SOFR printed 3.85% on 17 Sep, August CPI kept the tightening bias, and US 2Y is still making highs at 4.76 (packet 100th percentile, +57bp 1m, +9bp on 18 Sep). Inference: the hiking cycle and higher-yield trend persist; fading 99th-percentile UST yields or the modest post-peak easing in SR3 is premature while US inflation/labor/consumer/activity gauges remain 72/75/69/74. Expression: pay SOFR_2027-09 rather than chase already-stretched USDCHF. Unknown: CFTC/CME positioning and live (non-dashboard_v8) gauges.
own_pitch.thesis: FACT: The Fed delivered a 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00%, official SOFR is 3.85%, August CPI kept the tightening bias, US gauges are 72/75/69/74, US 2Y is 4.76 with a +57bp 1m impulse and a further +9bp on 18 Sep, and SR3 peaks at 4.755 in Sep-2027 then eases. INFERENCE: Price, policy and macro are aligned for continuation of higher US short-end rates; a fade of 100th-percentile yields right after a hike with still-hot gauges is the classic premature mean-reversion this seat rejects. The mispricing is the assumption that 4.755 is close enough to terminal that one should receive the peak or buy the post-peak dip. UNKNOWN: positioning, live (non-v8) gauges, NZ rates. Primary expression is pay SOFR_2027-09. Spot USDCHF/EURUSD confirms but is inferior.
own_pitch.mispricing: Market implies a ~90bp hiking remainder to 4.755% by Sep-2027 and then a small ease. That prices a nearly complete cycle just as realized overnight has only moved to 3.85% and as US inflation/labor/consumer have not rolled over. The fade camp treats 99-100th percentile UST yields as the opportunity. This seat treats those percentiles as the trend. Edge is further cheapening of SR3U7 (higher implied) if the peak is revised up or the ease is delayed, not carry from merely delivering the already-priced path.

conflict_synopsis.core_view: Post-hike US tightening and the UST yield uptrend persist; fading 100th-percentile yields or the modest SR3 post-peak ease is premature while US gauges stay hot.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: Next US CPI/labor or FOMC path revision that lifts the SR3 Sep-2027 peak above the packet 4.755 implied.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: US policy path re-prices Sep-2027 implied back toward overnight SOFR 3.85, or inflation and labor gauges both roll over with the tightening bias reversed.

opposing_pitches.stance_summary: Verified: SOFR 3.85% (2026-09-17), CORRA 2.29%, AONIA 4.35%; Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 16 Sep after >90% futures odds; CA-US 2Y is -140bp as of 17 Sep. Inference: the 149bp US-over-Canada 2Y yield gap is the holding-period engine, not a fade. Unknown: CFTC/CME positioning and NZ rates. Patient expression is pay CA 2Y / receive US 2Y (short CA-US_2Y). Long USDCAD is the spot alternative; rates own the discrepancy more cleanly.
opposing_pitches.thesis: Verified fact: US 2Y 4.76% versus CA 2Y 3.27% is a -140bp CA-US_2Y print after a delivered Fed hike and SOFR 3.85% reset, while CORRA overnight is still 2.29% and Dec 1m CORRA is only 2.58%. Inference: the market is inviting a negative-carry fade of Canada cheapness. Carry-is-king will not pay 3.27% to short 4.76%. Short CA-US_2Y receives the high yielder, pays the low yielder, and still has room for Canada to catch up along its own CORRA path. The energy-hike catalyst that would overwhelm this is weaker after the Saudi Oman workaround, not stronger. Unknowns: NZ rates, CFTC, live temperature-gauge vintages. Patient 3-month hold; paper books pay SOFR on the full $100m whether flat or not, so a 149bp yield gap that can also mean-revert from -140bp is a better use of the allocation than sitting flat.
opposing_pitches.mispricing: The fade of CA-US_2Y at -140bp is the mispricing: it treats a 5y 4th-percentile yield gap as a long-Canada duration signal while the policy path still pays ~149bp to receive US versus pay CA, and while Dec CORRA at 2.58% has not caught a delivered US hike that lifted SOFR to 3.85% and SR3 Dec to 4.32%. Statistical cheapness of CA versus US is the discovery flag, not a reason to own negative carry.

conflict_synopsis.core_view: The 149bp US-over-Canada 2Y yield gap is a patient positive-carry hold after a delivered Fed hike, not a negative-carry fade of a 4th-percentile spread.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: Delivered 16 Sep Fed hike and 17 Sep SOFR 3.85% reset versus a still-lagging CORRA strip, with the Saudi workaround reducing the oil-hike catalyst.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: CORRA/CA 2Y re-prices more than SOFR/US 2Y from the Canada side on energy pass-through, or US yields collapse while Canada stays the low-yielder.

opposing_pitches.stance_summary: Verified: Fed delivered 25bp to 3.75-4.00%, SOFR jumped to 3.85, SR3 still prices more tightening, and US gauges are hot versus a much easier CORRA 2.29 Canada with core near 2% and labor 38. Inference: the post-FOMC USD bid is a policy-gap story that is already more complete in EURUSD/USDCHF than in USDCAD, where 3M spot still shows USD lagging CAD despite an extreme CA-US 2Y gap. Unknown: CFTC/CME positioning and whether energy pass-through offsets the Saudi oil-tail reduction. Trade long USDCAD spot; do not dilute the USD view into a CAD cross.
opposing_pitches.thesis: FACT: Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00%; SOFR is 3.85; SR3 still prices additional tightening; US gauges are hot; CORRA is 2.29; Canada core is near 2% with labor 38; CA-US 2Y is -140bp at a 1y extreme; USDCAD 3M is still -1.25% log and only 74th percentile after a 5D post-FOMC catch-up. INFERENCE: USD versus CAD is the cleanest USD-spot expression of that policy/labor gap because EURUSD and USDCHF have already done more of the dollar work, AUDUSD still has a 2Y pickup and housing has not sold the pair, and USDJPY just printed a 1D z of 2.73 after a BoJ hike. UNKNOWN: positioning, and whether energy pass-through overwhelms the reduced oil-supply tail. A CAD cross adds EUR or AUD second-order risk the mechanism does not need. Long USDCAD; carry from 3.85 versus 2.29 supports holding through the SR3Z6 window while the seat otherwise pays SOFR on $100m even if flat.
opposing_pitches.mispricing: Spot USDCAD has not made the already-extreme CA-US 2Y/10Y and overnight gap. The market-implied assumption is that CORRA catch-up and energy risk cap the pair near the 74th percentile. That assumption is too tight if US front-end tightening continues and Canada labor/core stay softer. Percentile 74 is a discovery flag that the pair is not stretched long, not a mean-reversion signal.

conflict_synopsis.core_view: Post-FOMC US tightening versus an easier, labor-soft Canada is a USD-spot story still incomplete in USDCAD after EURUSD and USDCHF have already moved more.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: US data keeping SR3 hikes priced versus Canada core/labor that cap CORRA catch-up, with oil tails reduced rather than exploding.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: USDCAD back through the 2026-09-15 ECB fix 1.3919750411647458 with SR3Z6 no longer above overnight SOFR.

opposing_pitches.stance_summary: Do not fade US 2Y just because it prints a 252-day high: it sits on the live SR3 path after a delivered, pre-priced hike with still-hot US gauges. The stretched object with a reversal condition is Australia: AU 2Y 4.999 as of 2026-09-16 sits through live AONIA (overnight 4.35; Oct-26 4.565; Mar-27 4.86; path peak 4.945) after 16 Sep housing evidence that the tightening channel is already biting. Fade the remaining 21-51bp of priced RBA hikes in the AONIA strip, not AUDUSD.
opposing_pitches.thesis: FACT: 16 Sep housing evidence shows NSW stamp-duty -24 percent y/y, volumes -18 percent, Sydney/Melbourne >7 percent off peak while AONIA still prices Oct-26 4.565 and Mar-27 4.86 from overnight 4.35, and AU 2Y 4.999 sits through that path. INFERENCE: crowded extrapolation of inflation-gauge 82 plus the delivered Fed hike has overshot the RBA's remaining hike capacity now that the housing channel is binding; the extra 21-51bp should be faded. UNKNOWN: positioning and the next CPI vintage. This is not a US 2Y fade and not an AONIA-easing call.
opposing_pitches.mispricing: The market prices another +21.5bp by Oct-26 and +51bp by Mar-27 in AONIA, and AU 2Y 4.999 is 13.9bp through Mar-27 AONIA 4.86, after housing volumes and prices have already broken. The 99th-percentile AU 2Y rank is the discovery flag, not the thesis. The mispricing is remaining hike premium versus a working tightening channel, versus the live AONIA path.

conflict_synopsis.primary_trade: short AONIA_2026-10 (receive AONIA Oct-Nov-Mar strip / AU rates down)
conflict_synopsis.core_view: Fade remaining RBA hike premium in AONIA because housing is already biting and AU 2Y sits through the live path; do not fade path-consistent US 2Y on percentile alone.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: Australian housing/labor prints and RBA communication that the tightening channel is binding, so Oct-Mar AONIA hikes are not delivered.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: AONIA Oct-26 4.565 and Mar-27 4.86 hold or rise while housing/labor stop deteriorating, or a delivered October RBA hike reprices the strip higher.

opposing_pitches.stance_summary: Canada labor and core inflation cannot support the 122bp of additional tightening priced into CORRA_2027-09. The Fed hike and energy-pass-through narrative have built a full BoC hiking cycle onto an overnight CORRA still at 2.29 while CA labor is 38 and core is near 2%. Long duration on CRAU27 is the cleanest slowdown expression; short AUDUSD is the fallback stress expression if housing/inflation stagflation is preferred in spot.
opposing_pitches.thesis: The 2027 CAD policy path is a late-cycle policy-error price: 122bp of hikes onto labor 38 and core near 2%. Receive CRAU27. If domestic demand stays slack, implied CORRA 3.51 is too high even if the Fed stays restrictive and even if CAD spot is mixed by energy.
opposing_pitches.mispricing: CRAU27 implies 3.51 versus overnight CORRA 2.29 (+122bp). That gap prices a BoC hiking cycle the labor, consumer, and core-CPI evidence do not support. Energy pass-through is the priced excuse; Saudi extra crude via Oman already reduced the extreme oil-supply tail.

conflict_synopsis.core_view: Canada cannot deliver the 122bp of 2027 hikes priced into CRAU27 given labor 38 and core near 2%.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: CA labor/CPI or BoC communications that refuse to validate a 100bp-plus 2027 hiking cycle.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: CRAU27 implied rate through the packet 2028 peak near 3.655, or CA labor/activity re-accelerating with core moving well above 2%.

opposing_pitches.stance_summary: Restrictive policy is already biting in Canada’s labor and core inflation, yet MX CORRA still prices a full hiking cycle. Receive 2027 CORRA rather than fade CAD in spot.
opposing_pitches.thesis: FACT: CORRA overnight is 2.29 while CORRA_2027-06 implies 3.365. FACT: Canada core CPI is near 2%, headline 3%, labor gauge 38. INFERENCE: MX is pricing a hiking cycle Canada’s slack and core do not require, using the delivered Fed hike and BoC energy-pass-through language as the story. Receive 2027 CORRA so that a pulled hike path, not a CAD energy residual, is the P&L. UNKNOWN: whether energy pass-through becomes generalized and whether activity 66 stays firm enough for BoC to try the first hikes into year-end.
opposing_pitches.mispricing: About 107.5bp of 2027-06 hike premium and 136.5bp of 2028-09 terminal premium versus overnight 2.29, against core-near-2% and labor 38. That is more overnight-to-2027 hike premium than SR3 prices from SOFR 3.85, even though US gauges are hot and Canadian gauges are not.

conflict_synopsis.core_view: Canada is pricing a 100bp-plus CORRA hiking cycle the labor and core data cannot support; receive 2027 CORRA.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: Canadian labor/CPI and BoC communications that pull the Nov-26 to 2027-06 hike path.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: CORRA_2027-06 implied rate holding at or above the 2028-09 peak of 3.655, or BoC delivering the already-priced Nov/Dec hikes.

opposing_pitches.stance_summary: US inflation, labor, activity and consumer heat are still inconsistent with a SOFR path that peaks at 4.755 in 2027-09 and then eases through 2028. Pay SOFR_2027-09 (long implied rate at the packet 4.755 mid) rather than USD spot, because the mispricing is the policy path itself. Fact: Fed delivered 25bp to 3.75-4.00% and SOFR printed 3.85 on 2026-09-17. Inference: that first hike was a waypoint, not the terminal. Unknown: positioning.
opposing_pitches.thesis: FACT: the Fed has hiked to 3.75-4.00%, SOFR is 3.85, and US heat scores are 72/75/69/74. FACT: SR3 still peaks at 4.755 in 2027-09 and eases into 2028. INFERENCE: inflation persistence keeps the terminal and the duration of restraint higher than that strip. Express the view by paying SOFR_2027-09. UNKNOWN: positioning and the next inflation print's composition.
opposing_pitches.mispricing: SR3U7 at 4.755 prices only 90.5bp of remaining tightening from SOFR 3.85 and already allows a 2028 fade to 4.62. That is too little terminal and too early easing given still-hot US inflation, labor, activity and consumer gauges after a hike that was more than 90% priced going in.

conflict_synopsis.core_view: US heat and a just-delivered hike are inconsistent with a SOFR terminal of 4.755 that already eases in 2028.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: US inflation or labor data that keep the Fed hiking beyond the 4.755 2027-09 peak.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: SR3U7 implied rate back through the packet 4.58 6m mid, or a confirmed US labor/inflation cooldown.

opposing_pitches.stance_summary: Verified: New Zealand Q2 GDP printed 0.2% q/q and beat forecasts, parliament passed an India FTA covering about 95% of NZ exports, and NZDUSD sits at a 1y 12.9th / 5y 8.6th percentile after -3.90% 1m and -1.90% 5d while AUDUSD is only +0.20% 1m and AUDNZD is at a 5y 99.96th percentile. Inference: the market is still pricing an NZ labor/consumer recession (gauges 32/38) that the activity print and trade catalyst have already started to falsify, so the cleanest pro-cyclical expression is long the beaten-up NZD rather than paying already-hawkish US or CA STIR. Unknown: NZ policy path and CFTC/CME positioning are missing; temperature gauges are dashboard_v8 retained.
opposing_pitches.thesis: NZDUSD is pricing a New Zealand recession that the 16 Sep GDP beat and India FTA have already started to contradict, while US activity remains hot and the extreme oil-supply tail has been reduced. Growth, trade, and risk appetite are more resilient than a 5y-cheap NZD implies. The trade is long the cyclical that was sold, not mechanically long every high-beta currency: AUD is not cheap and Australia's housing channel is biting, and paying US or CA STIR fights curves that already embed large additional hikes.
opposing_pitches.mispricing: Market prices NZ-specific stagnation (NZDUSD 5y 8.6th percentile, AUDNZD 5y 99.96th) as if labor 32 / consumer 38 dominate. That assumption is inconsistent with a GDP beat, an FTA covering about 95% of NZ exports, US gauges still 69-75, and a reduced oil-supply tail. The mispricing lives in NZDUSD because NZ rates cannot be marked.

conflict_synopsis.core_view: NZDUSD is still pricing an NZ recession after a GDP beat and India FTA, so the cheapest cyclical is the cleanest pro-growth expression.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: NZ GDP beat plus India FTA transmission against a still-offered NZDUSD.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: NZ activity confirms the labor recession or NZD sells off with AUD in a renewed oil/USD shock.

opposing_pitches.stance_summary: Verified: CA-US 2Y is -140bp as of 2026-09-17, 1y percentile 3.77 and 5y percentile 4.31, while CORRA 2.29 versus SOFR 3.85 and CRA 2027 contracts already imply 84-130bp of Canadian hikes. Inference: that left-tail spread is a peer-normalized dislocation, not a cheap-because-it-fell screen, and should converge by Canada rates rising versus the US because BoC energy pass-through plus still-3% headline CPI make overnight 2.29 an unsustainable 2Y anchor after a known Fed hike. Unknown: CFTC/CME positioning, whether CA labor 38 versus US 75 is a new wider-spread regime, and any REER/PPP fair value (absent from the packet).
opposing_pitches.thesis: Canada is too cheap versus the United States on a peer 2Y spread that sits in the left tail of both the 1y and 5y distributions. That is a valuation statement with a policy-path closing mechanism, not a fade of a decline. Verified facts: CA-US_2Y -140bp on 2026-09-17; CORRA 2.29 versus SOFR 3.85; Fed hike delivered to 3.75-4.00%; CRA prices 84-130bp of hikes through 2027; Canada CPI 3% / core near 2%; BoC minutes flag energy pass-through. Inference: overnight 2.29 cannot remain the 2Y anchor once that hiking path or energy pass-through shows up in data, so the spread should rise (become less negative) via higher CA rates relative to US rates. The Jan-2025 analog at -145bp then +25bp over 3m is the working forward template. Unknowns that cap size: CA labor gauge 38 versus US 75 may justify a structurally wider gap; positioning is missing; gauges are repo-retained.
opposing_pitches.mispricing: Valuation anchor: 5-year CA-US 2Y distribution. Current -140bp is the 4.3rd percentile of that window and the 3.8th percentile of 1y, with CA-US 5Y/10Y also at the 1y 0.20th percentile. The market is pricing a peer relationship in which Canada stays ~140bp cheaper on 2Y despite CRA already implying a 2027 CORRA near 3.5-3.6 versus SR3 near 4.7-4.8. Convergence should begin now because the known Fed hike has already printed in SOFR 3.85 and the spread cheapened another 15bp in five days — the opposite of the CORRA hiking path starting to close the gap — while BoC energy-pass-through risk is live and Canadian headline inflation is still 3%.

conflict_synopsis.core_view: Canada is too cheap versus the US on 2Y (and 5Y/10Y) versus 1y and 5y history; the spread should rise as CORRA's already-priced hiking path and BoC energy pass-through close a post-hike overshoot.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: Canadian inflation/energy data or BoC follow-through that starts closing the 156bp CORRA-SOFR overnight gap already implied by 2027 CRA.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: CORRA 2027 implieds collapse toward 2.29 or Canada disinflates without energy pass-through, leaving the 5y-tail spread as the new regime.

opposing_pitches.stance_summary: Short AUDNZD. The intended Australia-versus-New Zealand differential is contaminated in USD pairs: AUDUSD is not stretched while NZDUSD mixes a delivered Fed hike into NZ weakness. Packet facts put AUDNZD at a 5y extreme after a 4.3% 1m squeeze that extended on 18 Sep after AU-negative and NZ-positive news. Verified: ECB spots, AONIA path, gauges, housing/GDP/FTA items. Inference: those catalysts should cap AUD versus NZD. Unknown: NZ policy/2Y, AUDNZD carry, CFTC positioning.
opposing_pitches.thesis: Verified fact: AUDNZD 1.2468 as of 18 Sep, 5y 99.96th after +4.27% 1m, with the 18 Sep +0.65% print coming after AU housing and NZ GDP/FTA items. Verified: AUDUSD not stretched; NZDUSD weak; AONIA still hiking; NZ rates missing. Inference: the market is still pricing NZ unique weakness versus AU even though incremental catalysts point the other way, so the clean expression is short AUD versus NZD in the cross. Unknown: NZ policy rate, AUDNZD carry, positioning. USD pairs would make the seat long or short the Fed path by accident.
opposing_pitches.mispricing: AUDNZD prices an AU-NZ growth/policy gap that the 16 Sep news flow no longer supports. Similar inflation gauges plus AU housing pain and NZ activity/trade positives should not coexist with a fresh 5y extreme in AUD. The 1m log z 2.84 is the discovery flag, not the thesis; the thesis is the sign error versus new information.

conflict_synopsis.core_view: AUDNZD at a 5y extreme after a 4.3% 1m squeeze is the wrong sign versus AU housing pain and NZ GDP-beat/FTA news; the AU-NZ view belongs in the cross, not USD pairs.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: AU housing channel biting against still-priced AONIA hikes, plus NZ Q2 GDP beat and India FTA failing to show up in AUDNZD.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: AUDNZD makes new highs because NZ labor/activity remains binding and FTA/GDP do not reprice NZD, or a pure USD bid moves both USD legs equally.
